_readme: ONE json per project and vendor: it drives step 2 (run_odb_tool.py), step 3 (LayerBuilder_pyansys.py)
and step 9 (level_bga_shadow.py). Keep it in YOUR project folder, not in the shared tool folder.
Copy this file next to your project inputs, rename it (e.g. TH5_SYE.json) and fill every 'path'.
Relative paths are relative to THIS json file; absolute paths are fine (inputs may stay where they are). {tool} = the 'ODB Modifying Tool' folder.
Keys starting with '_' are help text and are ignored by the program.
Run:  python run_odb_tool.py <this json>   (or set CONFIG_FILE at the top of run_odb_tool.py and press Run).
Questions the program cannot decide are asked in the terminal (options.interactive = true) or written to
open_questions_<project>_<vendor>.md next to this json (interactive = false). Answers are stored in 'answers'.

project._name: REQUIRED. Short project name, e.g. TH5. Used in output folder and file names.
project._vendor: REQUIRED. PCB vendor name, e.g. SYE. Used in output folder and file names.
project._output_job_name: Job name written inside the ODB++ (lower case, letters/digits/_). null = <name>_<vendor>.

vendor_odb._help: REQUIRED. Working-gerber ODB++ from the PCB vendor (.tgz/.tar.gz/.tar). Never modified.

vendor_stackup._help: REQUIRED. Vendor stackup (.xlsx/.xls/.csv). Thickness comes ONLY from this file.
vendor_stackup._thickness_column: REQUIRED in practice: the header text of the thickness column to use (all words must appear in the header), or a column letter like "R". Examples: "SYE Final Thickness", "Final Thickness". A human names it; left empty -> the tool asks.
vendor_stackup._thickness_unit: mil | um | mm. null = read from the header ('mil' in the header text) or asked.
vendor_stackup._sheet: null = the sheet whose copper count equals the ODB++ is found automatically.

design_material_table._help: REQUIRED. Design-team stackup with the FR4 material of every dielectric layer. Material, PP/core type, layer names, copper oz and function come from this file.
design_material_table._sheet: null = automatic (sheet with the same copper count as the ODB++).
design_material_table._material_column: null = the column whose cells match the material library names.
design_material_table._thickness_column: Optional. Only used to list vendor-vs-design thickness differences in the report.

material_library._help: REQUIRED for step 6. Full path of PCB_Material_Library.xml (Engineering Data library in the 'Material vendor' folder of the Suppliers share; %USERPROFILE% may be used in the path). Every FR4 of the design table must be in it. The materials of this board are embedded into the Mechanical v6 script; import the same file into Engineering Data.

step_2d_drawing._help: Optional. 2D board drawing used by LayerBuilder. Used to check that the ODB++ outline and the drawing are the same rectangle, and as an extra coverage region.

options._interactive: true = ask questions in the terminal; false = write open_questions_*.md and stop (for AI-driven runs).
options._pcb_step: null = automatic (only step, or the single-board step called pcb/unit/board/edit/orig). Otherwise the step name.

origin._mode: profile_lower_left = move the profile lower-left corner to (0,0) | keep = vendor coordinates | offset_mm = shift by offset_mm

options._write_dielectric_name: Write the FR4 material into the matrix DIELECTRIC_NAME of every PP layer.

coverage._resolution_mil: Render resolution. 1 mil = about 30 s per layer for a 420 x 400 mm board.
coverage._also_drawing_region: Also compute coverage inside the 2D drawing rectangle (step_2d_drawing).
coverage._extra_regions_mm: More rectangles: {"smb": [x0, y0, x1, y1]} in mm, final coordinates.
coverage._region_for_outputs: Which coverage goes into the CSV files: profile | drawing | a name from extra_regions_mm.

options._ansys_versions: Translators used for the closed-loop check. v251 = 2025 R1, v261 = 2026 R1. Both are required to PASS.
options._mechanical_script_template: v6 equivalent-material script copied into the output with the library materials of this board embedded. null = skip.
options._work_dir: Scratch folder (large). null = %TEMP%. Keep it off <cloud_sync_folder>.

output._root: Output parent folder (relative to this json). Each run creates a new sub-folder.
output._name_pattern: Sub-folder and ODB++ file name. {timestamp} = YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS, so runs never overwrite each other.

answers._help: Answers to the tool's questions, decided by a human. Format: "<question key>": "<chosen option>", plus "_note": "who decided, why, date".

layerbuilder._help: Step 3: python 1_Scripts/LayerBuilder_pyansys.py <this json>. Needs a PASS run of step 2.
layerbuilder._stackup_csv: null = the *_workinggerber.csv of the NEWEST run folder under output.root. Otherwise a path.
layerbuilder._step_file: null = inputs.step_2d_drawing.path (one planar face, lower-left corner at 0,0).
layerbuilder._output_scdocx: null = geometry/<project>_<vendor>_Stackup.scdocx next to this json. Never overwritten: an existing file stops the run.

leveling._help: Step 9: python 1_Scripts/level_bga_shadow.py <this json>. Levels the BGA-shadow Z displacement (least-squares plane) and reports the warpage.
leveling._z_unit: Unit of the exported displacement: mm | m | um. Must agree with the unit in the column header, e.g. 'Directional Deformation (mm)'.
leveling._xy_unit: Unit of the node coordinates in ds.dat: mm (NMM solver units) | m | um.
leveling._flip_z: true = multiply the displacement by -1 (e.g. to look at the board from the other side, as a measurement does). A human decides this.
leveling._value_column: null = automatic (the only value column, or the 'Directional Deformation' one). Set the header text when the file has several value columns.
leveling._mode: detrend = subtract the fitted plane (default) | rotate = rigid rotation of the point cloud.
leveling._method: OLS = least squares (default). RANSAC | Huber | Tukey = robust fits for measured data with outliers.
leveling._accept_warnings: The script exits with code 2 while a WARNING is open. Set true only after a human has read and accepted the warnings.
leveling._cases: One entry per exported result: {"name": "220C", "result": "results/220C/BGA_Z_Disp.txt", "dat": "results/220C/ds.dat"}. result = Mechanical export (node number + Z displacement), dat = ds.dat of the SAME solve.
leveling._differences: Optional, default none. {"name": "220C_minus_150C", "minuend": "220C", "subtrahend": "150C"} subtracts two cases node by node BEFORE leveling (warpage change between two temperatures).
